subject: Sandbox allowance and team bucket allocation — clarification and milestone top-up
messages:

Subject: Sandbox credits — how do team buckets work?

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — LaunchFoundry's cohort loved the latency numbers. Quick operational question on the sandbox credits: our program provides each startup with a single sandbox workspace, but many of the teams (3-6 people) want their own dev sub-workspaces. How are the complimentary sandbox credits consumed if we allocate multiple seats/sub-workspaces?

Specifically:
- Is usage charged to the parent workspace only, or can we create per-team buckets so each team gets an independent allowance?
- Do unused credits roll over between startups in the same cohort or are they isolated per account?
- If we need a one-time top-up tied to a cohort milestone (demo day), can Redwood do a promotional top-up that is conditional on hitting a usage milestone?

Appreciate any clarity here. We want to finalize the onboarding docs this week.

Best,
Ethan Cole
Director, Launch Programs
LaunchFoundry

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 16 Nov 2028 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sandbox credits — how do team buckets work?

Ethan — great question and glad the demo landed. Short answers up front, then a suggested operational model.

1) Consumption model: credits are consumed at the workspace level. You can create sub-workspaces, but by default all token consumption rolls up to the billing workspace unless you explicitly create separate billing scopes (we can do that for accelerator partners).

2) Per-team buckets: yes, we can provision per-team billing scopes tied to the parent accelerator account. That lets you give each startup (or each team within a startup) a fixed allowance. It requires a one-time config on our side and an internal tag for each scope so reporting shows per-bucket usage.

3) Rollovers: credits granted via the accelerator promo do not automatically roll between different customer accounts; they are scoped to the account or billing scope you choose at issuance. We can, however, create a pooled promo bucket at the cohort level that the program admin (LaunchFoundry) can reassign across teams — that would be an exception to our standard promo behavior and needs a short approval from finance.

4) Milestone top-ups: we support conditional one-time top-ups tied to milestones (e.g., demo day). Typical flow: you declare the milestone and criteria, we create a promo top-up token that is applied when you verify the milestone. We usually require a short MOU (one page) for auditability.

Proposed operational model (for your cohort):
- Create accelerator parent account A-LF-2028 as the program admin.
- Provision per-team billing scopes for up to 25 startups; each scope gets a default 100k token sandbox allowance.
- Create a pooled cohort promo bucket (20% of total) that LaunchFoundry can reassign; access controlled by program admin.
- Milestone top-up: conditioned on a short event verification form; one-time top-up of 50k tokens for demo-verified teams.

If that sounds good I can loop in Marissa for the promotional approval and Ben for billing ops to map the scopes. I attached a small dashboard snapshot to show how reporting would look per scope.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer

Date: Fri, 17 Nov 2028 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sandbox credits — how do team buckets work?

Hey Ethan — thanks for the clear ask. I'm comfortable approving a pooled cohort bucket as an exception for LaunchFoundry provided we document the assignment rules and expiration. A couple of notes on internal constraints:

- Promotional top-ups tied to milestones are approved case-by-case. For a cohort-wide program we typically cap the total promotional liability (so we don't open unlimited top-ups). For your size this would look like a capped pool and a per-team cap for demo top-ups.
- We'll need the LaunchFoundry MOU (1 page) and a short verification flow (Google Form or webhook) to trigger auto-application of the top-up. Finance wants a record so they can reconcile marketing/promos vs. actual consumption.
- For the per-team billing scopes: Ops can create them, but we need a single CSV mapping startup name -> email -> desired scope id before provisioning. Ben, can you confirm how long that provisioning takes?

Ethan — if you can send the mapping and the MOU draft (or let us use your standard MOU template), we can fast-track this. Happy to approve the pooled promo up to 500k tokens for the cohort with per-team demo top-ups capped at 75k tokens. If you need a higher cap we can escalate to finance for a one-off.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Ethan — quick operational notes from billing/ops side:

- Provisioning ETA: once we receive the CSV mapping we can provision up to 25 scopes in ~48 business hours. If you need them sooner, let us know which startups are highest priority and we can stagger provisioning.
- Alerts: we have a per-scope alerting hook that can 1) send emails to the founder contact, 2) post to a Slack webhook, or 3) call a customer webhook for custom flows. We will enable the 80% threshold by default for per-team scopes and you can change it via the cohort admin console.
- Promo expiry: 90 days is fine; we'll set the cohort pooled promo to expire automatically at T+90 from the cohort start date.

I'll attach the redlined MOU we typically use to make the approval easy; if LaunchFoundry's legal needs are significant we can route to our contracts manager.
